name: THE HIGH RIDGE
materialIdentity: The bare rock top of the ridge above the district, a cairn, a seat of rock, a survey pin; Consolation's lamps far below; night (errata 98, 99 E)
note: Room 29, doc 20: the high ridge, up the path from Sheng's door; the only place in the district with a view (doc 05).

LOOK_AT.say: A brass pin in the rock, set by the territorial survey. The one fixed point in the district. Everything below is measured, ultimately, from this.
repeat: Stamped with a number, a year, and a small arrow pointing at nothing in particular with great conviction.
Every deed in the valley, mine included, is a distance from this pin. It is the most important object in the district, and a goat could stand on it.

LISTEN_TO.say: Nothing. Fixed points have nothing to add.
repeat: Nothing. Brass in rock, holding still for everybody.
Nothing. It does not hum in the wind. It is the only thing up here that doesn't.

overrides.PULL: The one fixed point in the district. Prying at it felt like arguing with north.

LOOK_AT.say: From up here you can see the order they were built in. The saloon first. The assay office second. The schoolhouse third — before the church, before the bank, before anybody's house. They built a school for children who had not arrived yet, and no teacher ever came.
repeat: The schoolhouse roof has fallen in. Nobody has mended it, because nobody has had a reason to.
The church is fourth. The town found time to be good after it had found time to be drunk, assayed and educated.
Nothing. Twelve years of building make no sound from this high.
Nothing. A schoolhouse with no children in it is quiet even from close up.

LOOK_AT.say: A shelf of rock polished by a generation of sitting.
repeat: Below it the ledge is worn into two heel marks, where people have sat with their knees up and thought.
I sat. The town fit between my boots. It did not make the decision any smaller.
then: Whatever people come up here to decide, this is where they sit to decide it.

LISTEN_TO.say: The wind, divided around the rock.
repeat: The pocket of quiet behind the rock. You could hear a thought in it.
My own breathing, for once louder than the town.
then: Behind it, a pocket of true quiet — the only one for miles.

overrides.TALK_TO: I asked it what the others decided, all the ones before me. The quiet behind the rock kept every confidence. Good stone.

LOOK_AT.say: Eleven hundred miles that way. From up here you can see about nine of them.
repeat: The coach road, a pale thread going over the edge of the world. I came in on it.
From up here it looks almost walkable. That is the view's one lie.
Nothing coming.
Nothing coming.

LOOK_AT.say: A cairn of ridge stones, added to by everyone who ever climbed up here and felt something. It is taller than I expected.
repeat: Some of the stones have names scratched on them, some have dates. One has a single word, SORRY, and nobody has put a stone on that one.
I've added a stone. I didn't feel anything in particular. I added it anyway, in case.

LISTEN_TO.say: Stone on stone, holding. The wind takes the top note off it.
repeat: A stone settling, very slightly, under the weight of all the others.
The wind takes its note off the top, as before, and the cairn hums it back lower.

overrides.PICK_UP: You add. You do not subtract. I added.

LOOK_AT.say: Four hundred claims, laid out below like a badly ruled page.
repeat: From here you can see which ones are worked and which have been left. More have been left.
Mine is near the edge, beside the famous one. From up here they are exactly the same size, because they are.
then: Somewhere in the middle is forty feet that belongs to me.

LISTEN_TO.say: Nothing. Four hundred holes and not a sound out of any of them.
repeat: Nothing, and then, very faint, one pick somewhere. One man who has not given up.
Nothing. From up here the whole rush is a silent picture.

LOOK_AT.say: You cannot look at it, but up here you stand in it the way you stand in a river.
repeat: It leans on me with the full weight of the territory, and the territory is not light.
My coat has been trying to leave since I arrived. Up here it very nearly manages.
then: It has been traveling for a week and stops for nobody's hat.

LISTEN_TO.say: It says the one long thing it always says.
repeat: The same long thing. It has never needed a second subject.
A gust, a low whistle across the cairn, and then the long thing again.

LOOK_AT.say: All of Consolation at once: two streets, a steeple, the diggings' brown lace. From here it is exactly what it is — a stage set, assembled in a valley, waiting for its play.
repeat: The town, from above. From here you can see that every building on Main Street is a front with nothing behind it, and that people are moving between them anyway, briskly, all day.
I can cover the whole of Main Street with one thumb. The Colonel has a portrait that does the same to the East.

LISTEN_TO.say: Everything, faint and mixed. The bell, the picks, a dog.
repeat: Faintly, all of it at once. It sounds exactly like a real town.
The bell, a beat late, as if the sound had to climb.
then: The town's whole voice fits in a pocket up here.

overrides.USE: I used it the way everyone uses it: I stood in the wind until my problems reached their correct size, and then I climbed back down to them.
